hook.say: You pay a hundred rupees at a store.

hook.text: But your bank says ₹100 is gone.
hook.say: But your bank says a hundred rupees is gone.

hook.text: So you pay again. Now it's gone twice.

lost.text: Your request reached the bank, and the bank took the money.
But the response got lost on the way back.
The payment didn't fail. Your app just never heard back.

trap.text: A timeout isn't a failure. It's unknown.
But if the app retries it as a brand new payment,
the bank sees a new order, and charges you again.

key.text: The fix is an idempotency key.
When checkout opens, the app creates one unique key,
and sends that same key with every retry.
The server saves the key with the result.
Same key again? It replays the saved answer, and never calls the bank twice.

cases.text: Double tap? A unique constraint lets only one request win.
The second one waits for the first one's answer.
Bank too slow? Mark it pending, never failed.
A webhook or a reconciliation job settles it later.

takeaway.text: Retries are only safe when the operation is idempotent.
One checkout. One key. One debit.

cta.text: Try it yourself in Structura: drop the response and watch the retry.
